items.title: Modalities and dosage of exercise interventions for improving adolescent mental health: a systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Exercise can reduce depression, anxiety and stress in teenagers, with different types and amounts possibly helping different symptoms.
ai.summary: Researchers combined 17 randomised controlled trials of exercise programmes for adolescents. Exercise was linked to lower depression, anxiety and stress compared with control groups. The review suggests low-intensity TCC under three times a week for over 60 minutes may help generally, HIIT over 60 minutes under three times a week may help anxiety, and yoga for 30–60 minutes under three times a week may help stress.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that regular physical activity may be a useful, non-drug way to support teenage mental wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Try doing gentle movement such as yoga or tai chi a couple of times a week and notice whether your mood feels steadier.
ai.fact: Exercise interventions were linked to significant reductions in depression, anxiety and stress among adolescents in the included trials.

quiz.question: What did the review find about exercise and adolescent mental health?
quiz.answer: Exercise was linked to significant improvements in depression, anxiety and stress compared with control groups.

ai.caveat: The review included only 17 trials, results varied widely across studies, and publication bias cannot be ruled out, so the specific exercise recommendations should be treated as tentative.

items.title: Ergonomic interventions for treating work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder in adults.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Ergonomic changes may make little or no difference to arm, neck or shoulder pain in the short term.
ai.summary: This Cochrane review looked at 20 studies involving 2478 adults with work-related arm, neck or shoulder complaints. It found ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in pain, functional status or sick leave compared with no treatment, usual care or placebo in the short term.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people understand that adjusting a workstation alone may not quickly reduce work-related aches or time off work.
ai.life_skill: Try adjusting your desk, chair or equipment for comfort, but do not expect it by itself to cure arm, neck or shoulder pain.
ai.fact: Work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder can develop from repetitive movements, awkward postures or external forces such as vibrating tools.

quiz.question: What did the review find about ergonomic interventions and pain in the short term?
quiz.answer: They may result in little to no difference in pain compared with no treatment, usual care or placebo.

ai.caveat: The evidence is mostly low- to moderate-certainty and the abstract cuts off before reporting all results.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of recommended interventions for managing low back pain: A systematic review.

ai.headline: Non-drug, non-surgical low back pain treatments such as exercise, acupuncture and self-management support can be cost-effective compared with usual care.
ai.summary: The researchers reviewed 20 studies of guideline-recommended non-pharmacological, non-surgical treatments for low back pain. Most were cost-effective at a £20,000-per-QALY threshold, and some—including yoga, acupuncture, cognitive therapy and self-management support—were both more effective and less costly than usual care.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows which everyday back-pain options may offer better value for money, helping people and health services choose treatments that work without unnecessary cost.
ai.life_skill: Try asking a qualified health professional about exercise, self-management support or psychological support for ongoing low back pain instead of assuming medication or surgery is the only option.
ai.fact: Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide.

quiz.question: What did most of the reviewed low back pain interventions have in common regarding cost-effectiveness?
quiz.answer: Most interventions were cost-effective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of £20,000 per quality-adjusted life year.

ai.caveat: All the evidence came from high-income countries and was heterogeneous, so findings may not apply to low- and middle-income settings.

items.title: Factors Affecting Work Productivity and Activity Impairment in Axial Spondyloarthritis Patients

ai.headline: Axial spondyloarthritis is linked to high unemployment and activity impairment in Bangladeshi adults.
ai.summary: This cross-sectional study of 222 adults with axial spondyloarthritis found that 38.7% were unemployed and activity impairment was higher among unemployed participants. Disease activity, functional limitation and poorer physical health were linked to greater work productivity loss and activity impairment.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a chronic inflammatory condition can affect work and daily activity during economically productive years.
ai.life_skill: Notice how pain and physical health affect your ability to work or do daily tasks, and discuss them with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: In this study, 38.7% of participants with axial spondyloarthritis were unemployed.

quiz.question: What percentage of participants were unemployed in this study?
quiz.answer: 38.7% of participants were unemployed.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional study at one Bangladeshi centre, so it cannot prove causes and may not apply to other settings.

items.title: The effects of non-pharmacological school-based interventions on educational outcomes in children and young people with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analysis

ai.headline: School-based support may slightly improve educational outcomes for young people with ADHD, but results are mixed.
ai.summary: The study reviewed 16 randomised trials of school-based interventions for children and young people aged 5–17 with ADHD. Overall, the interventions showed a small effect on educational outcomes, but no specific type of intervention or outcome stood out as clearly better.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that schools can offer support for students with ADHD, but there is not yet enough clear evidence to know which approaches work best.
ai.life_skill: Talk to a teacher or school support staff about what help is available if you find learning difficult.
ai.fact: A meta-analysis combines results from multiple studies to look for an overall pattern.

quiz.question: What did the meta-analysis find about school-based interventions for young people with ADHD?
quiz.answer: Overall they showed a small effect on educational outcomes, but no particular intervention type or outcome domain was clearly better.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the included studies varied so much that the overall pattern is inconclusive.

items.title: Criterion validity of device-based motion sensors for monitoring free-living physical activity in community-dwelling manual wheelchair users: A systematic review
items.venue: European Journal of Adapted Physical Activity

ai.headline: Motion sensors can accurately track physical activity in people who use manual wheelchairs.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 40 studies of 34 devices that measure movement in manual wheelchair users. Sensors worn on the body or mounted on the wheelchair gave accurate estimates of energy use, self-propulsion, other activities, and wheelchair time, distance and speed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how activity can be measured fairly in wheelchair users, helping them and services track movement and health.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing how much you move each day, whether by wheelchair or otherwise, as part of everyday health.
ai.fact: Manual wheelchair users tend to be less active and more sedentary than people who walk.

quiz.question: What did the review find about body-worn tri-axial accelerometers on the upper arm or wrist?
quiz.answer: They provided the most accurate estimate of energy expenditure and helped tell self-propulsion apart from other daily activities.

ai.caveat: The evidence quality varied, with many devices rated low or very low, and the authors call for better-quality research.

items.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions

ai.headline: A new training method helps AI models see images more accurately by rewarding correct visual details.
ai.summary: The study tested PerceptRL, a way to train multimodal large language models to improve fine-grained visual perception. It converts verified errors from image captions into question-and-answer tasks with rule-based rewards, and adds multi-turn visual inspection for complex cases. On seven benchmarks, it improved average accuracy by 15.7 percentage points over a base model with the same tools.
ai.why_it_matters: Better AI vision could make everyday tools like image search and accessibility apps more reliable.
ai.life_skill: Check that AI descriptions of images match what you can actually see before relying on them.
ai.fact: PerceptRL surpassed the strongest evaluated frontier vision-language model by 5.2 percentage points on average accuracy across seven benchmarks.

quiz.question: What did PerceptRL use to turn image-caption errors into training tasks?
quiz.answer: It converted verified visual errors into QA pairs with fixed answer labels and rule-based rewards.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: A Polygenic Score for Smoking Persistence Captures Differences in Cessation Age

ai.headline: A genetic score linked to smoking persistence is associated with later quitting age across diverse groups.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 139,129 current and former smokers and compared those with the highest and lowest genetic scores for smoking persistence. People in the highest decile had an estimated median cessation age of 48 years versus 40 years in the lowest decile, an 8-year difference after adjustment.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how genetic liability may help identify people who could benefit from earlier, targeted support to stop smoking.
ai.life_skill: Notice if quitting feels harder for you and consider seeking tailored stop-smoking support early.
ai.fact: Earlier smoking cessation is linked to greater health benefits.

quiz.question: What was the adjusted median cessation age difference between the highest and lowest genetic score deciles?
quiz.answer: The highest decile had an estimated median cessation age of 48 years compared with 40 years in the lowest decile, an 8-year difference.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that the genetic score causes later cessation.

items.title: Cumulative heatwave exposure and cognitive ageing in Chinese middle-aged and older adults: educational vulnerability and urban concentration in a five-wave national cohort

ai.headline: More heatwave days are linked to faster cognitive decline in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, especially those with less education and urban residents.
ai.summary: Researchers followed over 13,000 Chinese adults aged 45 and older across five survey waves from 2011 to 2020. They found that each additional 10 heatwave days over the previous three years was linked to greater cognitive decline that grew stronger with age, with the effect concentrated among less-educated and urban participants.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how extreme heat may affect thinking skills as people age, highlighting groups that might need extra support during hot weather.
ai.life_skill: Check on older neighbours or relatives during heatwaves and help them stay cool and hydrated.
ai.fact: Heatwave days were defined as at least three consecutive days above the 92.5th percentile of the 1986–2005 temperature climatology.

quiz.question: Which group showed stronger heat-related cognitive ageing in the study?
quiz.answer: Less-educated adults and urban residents showed steeper heat-related cognitive ageing than others.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that heatwaves caused the cognitive decline.

items.title: Metabolomics in the wild: A scoping review of non-invasive methods for understanding vertebrate wildlife health and success

ai.headline: Scientists are increasingly using non-invasive samples to study the chemistry of wild vertebrate animals.
ai.summary: A scoping review of 83 peer-reviewed papers found that non-invasive metabolomics research on wild vertebrates has grown rapidly, with over 60% published between 2022 and 2025. The research covered 93 species, mostly mammals, and focused mainly on physiology, reproduction, diet and nutrition.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how new, animal-friendly lab techniques are helping conservationists understand wildlife health without harming the animals.
ai.life_skill: Notice how scientists study wild animals using samples like droppings or feathers instead of taking blood.
ai.fact: Most of the mammal species studied using non-invasive metabolomics are listed as at risk of extinction on the IUCN Red List.

quiz.question: What percentage of the reviewed papers were published between 2022 and 2025?
quiz.answer: Over 60% of all publications were published between 2022 and 2025.

ai.caveat: This is a scoping review summarising existing observational studies, so it maps the field rather than proving a single cause-and-effect finding.

items.title: University at Buffalo Campus Veggie Van Mobile Market

ai.headline: A mobile produce market on a university campus aims to improve student access to fresh fruit and vegetables.
ai.summary: This observational study will pilot a mobile market at the University at Buffalo to learn what stops students eating healthy foods, how to run the market to reach students, and whether using it is linked to eating more fruit and vegetables, better food security, and SNAP participation.
ai.why_it_matters: Food insecurity is common among students and can affect wellbeing and study, so finding practical ways to improve access to fresh food matters for everyday student life.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether easy access to affordable fresh produce changes what you eat.
ai.fact: Food insecurity affects first generation, lower-income, and racial/ethnic minority college students at higher rates.

quiz.question: What is the study trying to find out about a mobile market on campus?
quiz.answer: It aims to learn what makes healthy eating hard, how the market should operate, and whether market use is linked to eating more fruit and vegetables, food security, and SNAP participation.

ai.caveat: This is an observational study, so it can show links but cannot prove that the mobile market causes changes in eating or food security.

items.title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching

ai.headline: AI chatbots vary widely in how safely they coach sport and health, a new benchmark finds.
ai.summary: Researchers created MoveBench, a test for large language models in sports and health coaching. They tested 15 AI models on 809 questions using 5,012 rubric criteria covering safety, scientific validity and personalization. Performance varied widely, especially in safety awareness and program design.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI fitness and health advice can be inconsistent or unsafe, so people should not rely on chatbots alone for coaching.
ai.life_skill: Check any AI-generated exercise or health advice with a qualified professional before following it.
ai.fact: MoveBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models on sports and health coaching using safety, scientific validity and personalization criteria.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and it tests AI models rather than giving direct evidence about real-world coaching outcomes.

items.title: scTGCL: A Transformer-Based Graph Contrastive Learning Approach for Efficiently Clustering Single-Cell RNA-seq Data

ai.headline: A new computer method groups single cells more accurately by learning patterns in gene activity data.
ai.summary: The study tested scTGCL, a Transformer-based graph contrastive learning tool, on twenty real and simulated single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. It outperformed nine existing methods in clustering accuracy and related measures, while also being faster on large datasets and better at filling in missing gene activity values.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps scientists understand cell types and biological processes more reliably, which can improve research into health and disease.
ai.fact: Single-cell RNA sequencing measures gene activity in individual cells to reveal cellular diversity.

quiz.question: What did scTGCL do better than nine existing methods across twenty datasets?
quiz.answer: It achieved higher clustering accuracy, normalized mutual information, and adjusted Rand index, plus better imputation and faster runtime on large datasets.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are preliminary and not yet confirmed.

items.title: Comparative Advantage and Economies of Scale under Uncertainty -- by Xiao Ma, Natalia Ramondo

ai.headline: Uncertainty and economies of scale reduce the gains from trade by shifting jobs away from riskier places and sectors.
ai.summary: The paper uses a model of regional economies to study how uncertainty and economies of scale affect where people work and how much they gain from trade. It finds that uncertainty pushes employment away from riskier sectors and locations, lowering overall gains from trade by around 20 percent. Agglomeration forces and flexible labour supply can soften losses for regions that would otherwise lose from trade.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why economic shocks can reshape local job markets and why the benefits of trade are smaller when the future is uncertain.
ai.life_skill: Notice how uncertainty in your local job market might affect your career choices and consider building flexible skills.
ai.fact: Uncertainty shifts employment away from riskier sectors and locations relative to a deterministic benchmark.

quiz.question: By roughly what percentage does uncertainty lower the U.S. aggregate gains from trade in the study?
quiz.answer: Around 20 percent.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and relies on a calibrated model rather than direct experimental proof.

items.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought

ai.summary: The study compared how brain signals linked to recognising faces develop in autistic and neurotypical children. It found these signals become more specialised as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children.
ai.why_it_matters: This may help explain why some autistic people find recognising faces and reading emotions difficult.

ai.fact: Brain signals associated with recognising faces become more specialised as neurotypical children grow older.

items.title: Workplace ergonomics may do little to ease arm, neck or shoulder pain

ai.summary: An updated Cochrane review looked at ergonomic interventions for workers with arm, neck or shoulder complaints. It found no meaningful benefit for pain, function, recovery or sick leave compared with no treatment.
ai.why_it_matters: People may spend time and money on workplace equipment expecting pain relief, but the evidence suggests it may not help.
ai.life_skill: Try focusing on movement habits and rest breaks rather than relying only on ergonomic equipment.
ai.fact: Ergonomic interventions showed no meaningful benefit for pain, function, recovery or sick leave in workers with work-related arm, neck or shoulder complaints.

quiz.answer: No, the review found no meaningful benefit for any of these outcomes.

items.title: DNA analysis identifies root-dwelling fungi as potential keystone species in forest microbial communities

ai.headline: DNA analysis suggests root-dwelling fungi may be keystone species in forest soil ecosystems.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed DNA from soil and root systems to study microbial communities in forests. They identified root-dwelling fungi as potential keystone species that disproportionately influence nutrient cycling and carbon sequestration.

items.title: The Relationship between Students' Perceptions and Their Engagement through Self-Regulated Learning

ai.headline: Students who manage their own learning better engage more in difficult statistics classes.
ai.summary: This study surveyed 533 psychology students in Indonesia to see how teacher creativity and self-regulation affect engagement in statistics. It found that self-regulated learning acts as a key link, meaning students who actively manage their learning process engage more deeply than those who do not.

items.title: Tracking West Nile virus dynamics using viral loads from trapped mosquitoes

ai.headline: Mosquito viral load data can reveal which West Nile virus carriers are likely infectious, improving public health risk estimates.
ai.summary: Researchers examined West Nile virus genetic material in trapped mosquitoes using PCR cycle threshold values from pooled samples. This could improve how health agencies estimate transmission risk from mosquito surveillance.
ai.why_it_matters: Better surveillance estimates could help public health teams target mosquito control more accurately and reduce human exposure to West Nile virus.

items.title: Mind–body reprogramming therapy: development, theoretical foundation, and clinical application for Long COVID

items.title: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior

ai.headline: Fetuses who sleep more at night in the womb tend to keep that pattern after birth.
ai.summary: Researchers monitored 32 mother-child pairs using wearables to track fetal movement and maternal activity during the third trimester. They found that fetuses showing a preference for sleeping at night were more likely to maintain that sleep pattern in their first six months of life.
